messages:
ingrid: quick summary from today's profiling run — we have recurring p99s on long-sequence requests (>=1024 tokens) even though p95 is fine. looks like kv-cache eviction + kernel fallback are showing up as tail contributors.
maurice: sending flamegraphs + kernel-selector logs: https://redwood.internal/prof/1784023456 (ptal) :mag_right:
maurice: attach: `flame_cpu_seq1024.svg`
jamie: short take: two separate issues — 1) microbatching groups long requests and triggers kv churn, 2) for some model variants the selected matmul kernel is causing a synchronous fallback path that adds ~200ms for some shards.
sherna: can you paste the numbers? what are p95/p99 and qps delta when we change microbatch size?
ingrid: quick table from bench run (mb = microbatch size):
```
mb=16 -> p95=120ms, p99=480ms, qps=540
mb=8  -> p95=140ms, p99=220ms, qps=440
mb=4  -> p95=200ms, p99=260ms, qps=300
```
ingrid: so smaller microbatches reduce tail but cost throughput. p99 drops a lot at mb=8.
ajex: @alex (typo) — oops
alex: haha. ok. comment: the kernel fallback we saw triggers when sequence length + kv hits > certain workspace. the selector currently prefers faster avg throughput kernel, but its variance is high for long sequences.
jamie: idea: selector should be latency-aware per-seqlen bucket. prefer stable kernel for >512 tokens even if average is slightly slower.
sherna: that could help p99. how about server-side truncation/timeouts as a guardrail for apps that submit extreme lengths? we keep SLOs for platform.
ingrid: prototype policy I ran: requests with declared max_tokens > 1024 get soft-truncated to 1024 unless the caller has high-tier flag. combined with microbatch cap of 8 for seq>512. result: p99 drops ~35% across cluster.
maurice: profiling details: KV eviction rate drops by 60% under that policy, KV cache hit spikes from 78% -> 92% for steady-state traffic.
jamie: tradeoff: some apps get silently truncated. we should return a structured hint so callers know truncation occurred and can retry with an opt-in parameter.
alex: agreed. return header `x-rw-truncated: true` + body field `truncated_to: 1024` and reason. also emit metric `truncation.count` with tag tier.
sherna: what about timeouts? we currently have a generous 90s RPC timeout for generation. For long tail mitigation probably need a request-level timeout of 25s and a hard cap at 60s for non-enterprise customers.
ingrid: tested 25s cap on a sample traffic slice: p99 300 -> 190ms (for shorter seqs) because the scheduler stops trying to salvage ultra-long-running shards. it also stabilizes slot occupancy.
perf-bot: sched:slot_utilization decreased from 78% -> 72% after timeout policy (observed window 30m)
maurice: can we make the microbatching dynamic — i.e., if a queue has many long requests reduce batch cap, otherwise use higher cap? that preserves throughput for short-request heavy queues.
jamie: yes, propose: dynamic microbatcher with two dimensions: per-worker long_seq_ratio and global latency pressure flag. policy: if long_seq_ratio > 0.25 -> mb_cap=8 else mb_cap=16. if global latency_pressure -> mb_cap = max(4, current_mb_cap/2).
ingrid: added config prototype in runtime flags:
```
microbatch:
  default_cap: 16
  long_seq_threshold: 512
  long_seq_ratio_trigger: 0.25
  cap_under_pressure: 4
  scale_down_factor: 2
```

alex: also change kernel selector heuristics: maintain per-kernel p99 estimate for seq buckets (<=256, 257-512, 513-1024, >1024) and pick kernel with lowest p99 instead of lowest mean when latency SLOs are enabled. we can fall back to mean for throughput-heavy tiers.
sherna: ops note: need rollout plan. don't flip heuristics cluster-wide. recommend canary in single region with `latency_slo_mode=true` flag for a week, track model-specific regressions.
jamie: add automated eval: run prompt set of 50 long prompts against canary every 4h and compare quality/regression. don't want to degrade output due to kernel change.
ingrid: also want to protect clients from silent truncation — add a client-side advisory in SDKs + response code 206 with a `truncated` field.
maurice: one more wrinkle — some customers use function-calling and expect deterministic end-of-generation. truncation can break those flows. we should allow `allow_truncate=false` header to opt-out but that puts them on higher-latency SLO class and they might get 413 after timeout.
alex: implement quota for opt-outs: they consume burst tokens from Dedicated pools. that way we avoid noise on shared pools.
jamie: next actions: 1) ingrid + maurice finalize dynamic microbatch config prototype and kernel p99 metrics, 2) sherna draft rollout + opt-out policy, 3) alex update SDK response pattern and header, 4) ops run 24h canary with perf-bot alerts.

ingrid: thanks. I'll post a follow-up with the canary manifest and the perf dashboards to watch (p95/p99 by seq-bucket, kv hit rate, microbatch cap distribution).
sherna: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary cluster create request accepted (id: canary-178402)
perf-bot: monitor: p99_long_seq decreased by 36% in canary after initial config (12h window)
maurice: great start, we should keep an eye on quality regressions.
jamie: logging to add: kernel_selector.choice and kernel_selector.p99_estimate tags on every request in canary. keep logs lightweight.
ingrid: putting tasks into sprint board under ENG-RUNTIME -> SLA-TAIL-GUARDRAILS.
